headline: US stocks ended lower to start Q3 as semiconductor profit-taking and softer labor data offset ongoing manufacturing expansion and cautious Fed messaging
raw_text:
- Major US indices closed mixed with the Nasdaq leading declines on chip-stock weakness, while financials, banks and select consumer and communication-services names outperformed
- ISM manufacturing PMI came in at 53.3 for June, marking a sixth straight month of expansion but missing expectations and indicating slower growth with easing input and price pressures
- ADP (ADP) private payrolls added 98,000 jobs, below forecasts, keeping focus on Friday’s official June jobs report for confirmation of labor-market cooling
- Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation risks had faded compared with recent weeks but remained too high, reaffirming the 2% goal while avoiding direct guidance on a July rate move and reinforcing rotation away from overheated tech
- Semiconductor names led losses, with Micron Technology (MU), Sandisk (SNDK) and Intel (INTC) down sharply and Nvidia (NVDA) and Broadcom (AVGO) also weaker on profit-taking after strong first-half gains
- Caterpillar (CAT) fell nearly 7% amid reports that Michael Burry expanded AI-related short bets tied to the name
- General Mills (GIS) gained roughly 8% after beating fiscal Q4 estimates and outlining a $3B cost-savings plan with a cautious 2027 outlook
- Meta Platforms (META) jumped about 9% on reports it is building a cloud business to monetize excess AI computing capacity
- New IPO Bending Spoons (BSP), owner of AOL and Vimeo, surged nearly 40% in its Nasdaq debut after pricing at $29 a share and closing around $40.50
- After-hours trading saw muted earnings reactions, with FactSet (FDS) moving modestly higher after estimate beats and only select small-cap and penny IPO names showing notable follow-through
